decision_reason: The NASA-hosted repository is a public collection of Open MCT plug-ins and NASA research documentation links to this exact repository, but no root-level grant or clearly scoped license was found for this collection. The broader Open MCT license cannot be assumed to cover these separately maintained plug-ins; keep on hold pending an exact project/component grant and clarified product-family scope.

government_provenance.note: NASA NTRS paper on mission-operations software explicitly identifies and links the Open MCT Plug-Ins project/repository; the NASA GitHub organization hosts the exact source.

public_source.note: Public repository contains source plug-ins and README/build guidance for use with MCT; the linked parent MCT repository is currently unavailable, so this does not establish present end-to-end compatibility.

eligible_license.note: Repository review found no root LICENSE, LICENSE.txt, or COPYING grant. Do not transfer the separate Open MCT Apache-2.0 grant to plug-in code without component-level evidence.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's technical paper names the Open MCT plug-in repository and describes its role in mission-operations applications; the exact-product license and current parent compatibility remain unresolved.

product_identity: Open MCT legacy plug-in collection; a component family for the separate MCT framework, not the Open MCT core product
agency: NASA Ames Research Center (Open MCT program; exact collection sponsorship not fully resolved)
geography: United States federal mission-operations software research
license: Unresolved; no repository-level license grant verified for the plug-in collection
status_note: Hold: NASA documentation links this exact legacy component collection, but current exact-product support/parent parity and license scope are unverified.

decision_reason: NASA GSFC's exact Memory Dwell application is publicly distributed in the cFS repository, with user-guide build instructions and an Apache-2.0 root grant. The first verified grant-bearing source snapshot is 2020; the app is a distinct cFS application, separate from the cFS framework and its dependencies.

government_provenance.note: NASA TTP identifies the Core Flight System Memory Dwell application, explains its CPU-memory monitoring purpose, and its Download Now link resolves to this exact nasa/MD repository; the README attributes cFS to NASA Goddard Space Flight Center.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Memory Dwell C application and documentation/build files. Its user guide can be generated with the documented Doxygen make commands; cFE, OSAL, PSP, and cFS framework dependencies are separate.

eligible_license.note: The repository root grant is the OSI-approved Apache License 2.0 for this application source; do not extend it to separately distributed cFS dependencies.

primary_evidence.note: The current NASA software record names this exact application and current version 2.3.2, provides a direct download to its canonical repository, and documents function and Linux release details.

product_identity: NASA cFS Memory Dwell (MD) application, a reusable CPU memory-address monitoring/debugging app; not the cFS platform itself
geography: United States federal flight-software and spacecraft systems engineering
license: Apache-2.0 for the MD application repository; cFS framework, OSAL, PSP and third-party dependencies have separate licenses
status_note: Maintained: current NASA TTP GSC-18450-1 links this exact source and identifies version 2.3.2; the repo documents the app-specific user guide and framework dependencies.

decision_reason: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center developed and released this reusable mesh networking system. Its repository contains a NOSA 1.3 grant naming the exact MFS-33391-1 product, full documentation, and evidence of flight testing; the first verified grant-bearing public source is from 2017.

government_provenance.note: NASA TTP identifies the Mesh Network Communication System as MFS-33391-1 and describes the NASA product; the repository's NOSA identifies Marshall Space Flight Center as the originating government agency.

public_source.note: Public repository contains the mesh networking system source, dependencies, and full documentation; README describes small-satellite formations and flight-tested small-UAS deployments.

eligible_license.note: The exact project LICENSE is NASA Open Source Agreement Version 1.3, identifies NASA MSFC and designation MFS-33391-1, and grants worldwide rights.

primary_evidence.note: NASA technical paper describes the mesh network system and its demonstrated network architecture; NASA TTP MFS-33391-1 independently identifies the exact released product.

product_identity: Mesh Network Communication System, reusable peer-to-peer network architecture for small spacecraft and other vehicle/ground nodes
geography: United States federal aerospace communications and small-satellite research
license: NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3, specific to the Mesh Network Communication System (MFS-33391-1)
status_note: Maintained: repository has current source activity (2026-09) and NASA's official catalog continues to distribute the exact product; README links full documentation and describes flight-tested use.

decision_reason: NASA JPL's MISR program identifies MINX as a stand-alone analysis tool for plume heights and motion, links the exact GitHub release, and the public repository includes BSD-3-Clause source, binaries, and run/build instructions. A NASA-published 2024 study documents MINX scientific use; the 2016 v4.0 release is the first verified source snapshot carrying the project grant.

government_provenance.note: NASA JPL's current MISR Get Data page describes MINX's exact plume-height function and links its GitHub distribution; the NASA NTRS study identifies it as developed at JPL.

public_source.note: Public repository includes IDL application source, web documentation, OS-specific executable distributions, and explicit source run/build instructions.

eligible_license.note: The project LICENSE.txt contains the BSD 3-Clause grant for the MINX source; copyright is attributed to Caltech/JPL based on government-sponsored research.

primary_evidence.note: NASA NTRS-hosted 2024 research paper names MINX as the stand-alone JPL-developed software used to determine plume altitude and motion and links its release page; NASA's current MISR page independently documents and distributes the exact tool.

product_identity: MISR INteractive eXplorer (MINX), standalone IDL visualization and analysis software for aerosol-plume/cloud heights and motion
geography: United States federal Earth-observation science (NASA JPL/Caltech)
license: BSD 3-Clause for MINX source; bundled proprietary IDL runtime, if used, remains separately licensed
status_note: Maintained by current official distribution: NASA JPL's MISR Get Data page still identifies and links the exact project. The cited 2024 science paper confirms current scientific use; v4.1 is the latest posted release (2019), so this is not a claim of recent code activity.

decision_reason: NASA JPL's current MISR data page identifies the MISR Toolkit as reusable command-line and API software for MISR L1/L2 products, links the exact repository, and documents the supported language bindings. The repository has a BSD-3-Clause grant and extensive user/function documentation; the first verified grant-bearing source snapshot is 2020.

government_provenance.note: NASA JPL identifies the MISR Toolkit and links the exact nasa/MISR-Toolkit repository as official software for MISR products.

public_source.note: Public C source and Python, IDL, and C bindings are accompanied by installation/build guidance, examples, API documentation, release source archives, and offline docs.

eligible_license.note: Root LICENSE is BSD 3-Clause for the Toolkit source, with Caltech/JPL attribution and government-sponsored research statement; dependencies and bundled third-party libraries are separate.

primary_evidence.note: NASA JPL page describes Toolkit functions, supported C/Python/IDL access, and direct GitHub availability; the GitHub release page provides versioned source/binaries and installation details.

product_identity: MISR Toolkit, a reusable API/utility suite for accessing, manipulating, and reading MISR satellite standard products
geography: United States federal Earth-observation science (NASA JPL/Caltech)
license: BSD 3-Clause for MISR Toolkit source; third-party dependencies and binaries are separately licensed
status_note: Maintained: current NASA JPL data/software pages link this exact Toolkit, and repository source activity continued into 2026. NASA releases provide versioned installation packages and documentation.
